summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic pancreatitis and a Hickman line for TPN was admitted with fever, chills, and nausea, atypical of her usual flares. Initial labs showed acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, which resolved with IV fluids. Blood cultures identified Candida parapsilosis, indicating candidemia, with the Hickman line suspected as the source. The line was removed, and she was treated with IV micafungin, later transitioned to oral fluconazole. Echocardiogram and eye exam were normal. She remained stable, afebrile, and tolerated oral intake. She was discharged home on a 14-day course of fluconazole with follow-up plans for surveillance cultures and eventual re-evaluation for TPN line placement. Chronic pancreatitis, GERD, and anemia were managed supportively.
